# hubspot_property_group (Resource)

Manages a HubSpot CRM property group — a named section that organizes properties in the HubSpot UI. Property groups are referenced by `hubspot_property` via `group_name`. Requires the `crm.schemas.{objectType}.write` scope for the target object type (e.g. `crm.schemas.contacts.write`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Manage a custom property group on contacts. Properties created with
# hubspot_property can reference it via group_name.
resource "hubspot_property_group" "example" {
  object_type = "contacts"
  name        = "my_group"
  label       = "My Group"

  # Optional: position of the group in the HubSpot UI (lower sorts first).
  display_order = 5
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `label` (String) Human-readable label shown in the HubSpot UI. Can be changed in place.
- `name` (String) Internal (immutable) name of the property group. Changing this forces replacement of the group.
- `object_type` (String) CRM object type the group belongs to — an object type name such as `contacts`, `companies`, `deals`, `tickets`, or a custom object `objectTypeId` (`2-XXXX`). Changing this forces replacement of the group.

### Optional

- `display_order` (Number) Position of the group relative to other groups in the HubSpot UI (lower values sort first). Can be changed in place. If omitted, the server-assigned value is used.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite identifier in the form `{object_type}/{name}`, e.g. `contacts/my_group`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Property groups are imported using "{object_type}/{name}".
terraform import hubspot_property_group.example 'contacts/my_group'
```
